notes.text: Typescript leaf with running head - IV- 1102 -, the 1102 entered by hand. Archive pencil number 18 is recorded only as a comment. The supplied source is scan 19 and H calls it page 18. There is no date or independent title on this leaf.

Section (21.6.5) associates an effective divisor D with the closed subscheme Y(D) cut out by its invertible ideal and describes the converse for a regularly immersed closed subscheme of codimension one. It then forms a codimension-one cycle from lengths of the local rings of Y(D). Proposition (21.6.6) states additivity of this association on effective divisors and reduces the proof to an identity of module lengths.

The margin explicitly says “réf !”, with réf underlined. The other slanted note tentatively reads “devrait figurer|passer dans 21.2.” followed by the staggered groups “hyp.”, “(sans”, “noeth.)”. Its exact verb and compressed abbreviations remain doubtful; its apparent relocation proposal is a reading of the note, not an established editorial decision.

All visible crossed and overwritten groups are retained, including the two distinct qu groups, the long deletion after car, the underlying g in points, the noetherian condition, the changed initial L, and the small terminal punctuation after cyc(D). Heavy cancellations are not treated as securely recovered words merely because proposed restorations are grammatical.

The opening D may carry a prime although subsequent formulas in that sentence use D without one. The codim singleton was checked against H’s closure bar and no bar is visible. The sum does carry a detached prime. None of these was normalized according to mathematical expectation.

An equality sign is printed at both sides of one physical line turn, and an addition sign at both sides of another. These are retained in the diplomatic transcription, with an allowed break between the repeated signs. The length computation below treats them as line-continuation notation.
The last sentence stops after “on”. No completion or ellipsis has been supplied.

The whole image and each supplied half were viewed once. Eighteen targeted crops were generated with the supplied Pillow script and each viewed once. No OCR, recognition engine, external source, other page, other reader file, or root decision was consulted.

math_checks.claim: The module isomorphism used in the proof
math_checks.performed: Defined multiplication by t from A/t\prime A to tA/tt\prime A. It is well-defined since t(t\prime b) lies in tt\prime A and surjective by definition. If ta lies in tt\prime A, write ta=tt\prime b; regularity of t gives a=t\prime b, so the kernel is zero.
math_checks.result: This directly verifies the displayed isomorphism under the stated regularity assumption.
math_checks.limits: This does not verify the earlier cited sections or the geometric correspondence.

math_checks.performed: Used the natural surjection A/tt\prime A -> A/tA. Its kernel is tA/tt\prime A, giving a short exact sequence. For finite lengths, additivity and the preceding multiplication isomorphism give length(A/tt\prime A)=length(A/tA)+length(A/t\prime A).
math_checks.result: The algebraic step is consistent with the written proof. The repeated plus at the physical line turn is treated as a continuation sign, not an additional operation.
math_checks.limits: Finiteness of these lengths is assumed from the page’s one-dimensional local setting; no external proof or cited text was consulted.

math_checks.claim: Minimal support points of the effective divisor have codimension one
math_checks.performed: Checked the standard local reduction: a local defining non-zero-divisor t lies in no minimal prime; a prime minimal over the principal ideal (t) therefore cannot have height zero. Together with the principal ideal height bound in the noetherian setting, this gives height one.
math_checks.result: The dimension/support assertions fit the stated hypotheses and explain why only codimension-one support contributes to the sum.
math_checks.limits: This is a local reasoning check using the usual height bound, not a fresh proof of that bound, the regular immersion criterion, or the cited (19.1.4)/(21.2.7).

math_checks.claim: Closure bar and initial prime textual consistency
math_checks.performed: Compared the actual codim singleton and the cycle singleton strokes, then compared the first divisor’s small mark with the later unprimed D occurrences.
math_checks.result: The codim singleton lacks a bar, the cycle singleton has a bar, and the opening D mark remains uncertain. These were retained as separate ink readings.
math_checks.limits: No mathematical expectation was used to add the missing bar or remove the possible initial prime.

math_checks.performed: Read the references (21.2.7), (19.1.4), and (21.2.5) and the asserted identity I_X(D+D\prime)=I_X(D)I_X(D\prime).
math_checks.result: These statements and reference numbers were transcribed only.
math_checks.limits: The referenced sections were not supplied in the allowed inputs and were not checked. No global theorem verification is claimed.
